title: Graceful Interrupt shim for Go streaming: ergonomics, examples, and backpressure guidance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a small, well-tested Interrupt shim and example patterns for the Go SDK streaming API that make it ergonomic to cancel/timeout streaming reads while preserving backpressure guarantees, avoiding resource leaks, and documenting trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Interrupt shim exported as stream.Interrupter with a minimal API that wraps existing Reader/Iterator types
SDK examples directory contains two end-to-end examples: client-side cancel and server-side short-circuit handling
Unit and integration tests that simulate abrupt client cancellation, deadline expiry, and library shutdown without goroutine leaks
Benchmarks showing <5% p95 latency change for common short streams when shim is enabled
Documentation page in the Go SDK doc site with recommended patterns and anti-patterns
steps: Design API: small wrapper that exposes Cancel(), CancelWithErr(err), and Done() chan for select patterns
Implement internal stream.CancellableIterator that composes context.Context and an internal stop channel
Add backpressure safety: ensure Cancel does not drop unread messages from the transport; Cancel signals consumer to stop reading but lets in-flight work drain
Add tests: unit for shim, integration against streaming harness, leak-check (goleak) test
Create examples in examples/streaming/interrupt-shim and record a short demo script
Benchmark: microbenchmark for 1-token, 128-token, 1024-token streams comparing baseline vs shim
Docs: write usage guide, pitfalls, and pattern snippets for SDK docs and release notes
Code review and iterate based on feedback from infra and SDK owners
decisions: Expose minimal surface area to keep ergonomics simple; avoid embedding complex retry logic in the shim
Use composition with context.Context instead of creating new cancellation primitives to play well with user's request contexts
Design CancelWithErr to allow descriptive cancellation reasons (useful for observability) rather than only boolean cancel
Do not change transport semantics: shim will not auto-resume or replay messages — explicit API for replay will be a follow-up
risks: Developers may misuse Cancel() and expect automatic graceful drain — mitigated by docs and examples
Small increase in code complexity for stream types; risk of regressions on edge-case deadlines
Potential for minor latency overhead in thin streams; mitigated by benchmarks and opt-out in hot paths
comments: 2025-02-10 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after spike showed repeated patterns across clients where cancellation caused goroutine leaks. Spike notes attached to Confluence.

2025-02-12 - Marco Rivera: Implemented initial Interrupter interface in a branch. Basic cancellation semantics work; observed a race when Cancel() is called concurrently with the transport's read loop. Adding channel handshake to fix.

2025-02-14 - Code review (Erin Cho): Suggested renaming CancelWithErr -> AbortWithReason for clarity, and adding observability hook to emit telemetry on cancellations. Agreed to keep CancelWithErr for backward-compat with internal examples; add observability via optional callback.

2025-02-17 - Infra feedback (Diego Morales): Run go test -race and goleak; found leak in integration test where transport goroutine wasn't signalled on Cancel when Close() is delayed. Patch submitted to ensure transport Close() is called after handshake completes.

2025-02-20 - Marco Rivera: Added examples (examples/streaming/interrupt-shim) showing idiomatic usage with context.WithTimeout, select over Done(), and using AbortWithReason for metrics. Updated docs draft.

2025-02-25 - QA (Nina Gupta): Integration scenarios pass; benchmark shows 3.2% median latency overhead on microbench for 1-token streams and negligible for longer streams. Added note in PR about opt-out for extreme low-latency customers.
2025-02-28 - Asha Patel: Merged design doc updates and addressed Erin's review. Preparing final PR for mainline; will schedule a sweep to update release notes and examples in the website.
